in_text_mentions: A 28-year-old man was brought to our emergency department because of transient loss of consciousness and cyanosis. He was immediately intubated without concomitant drug administration and ventilated with 100% oxygen. Heart rate was 72 beats/min and blood pressure was 82/50 mmHg; oxygen saturation was undetectable on pulse oximetry. His Glasgow Coma Scale score was 3 and he had blue-gray discoloration of the skin, particularly of the face and nail beds (Figure 1).

panels.figure_caption: Arterial blood sample obtained in the emergency department, demonstrating a dark, chocolate-brown discoloration characteristic of methemoglobinemia. This abnormal hue results from oxidation of hemoglobin iron to the ferric (Fe3+) state, impairing its ability to bind and deliver oxygen.
in_text_mentions: A second ABG was obtained while on 100% FiO2 via HFNC, due to ongoing hypoxia and diagnostic uncertainty. Arterial blood appeared dark brown in color. These findings confirmed the diagnosis of methemoglobinemia (Table 2).

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of the face showing marked bluish-purple discoloration of the lips in a patient whose article title and in-text description establish methemoglobinemia (nail polish remover induced). The caption 'Cyanosis of the lips' plus the in-text description of blue-to-black discoloration of lips and tongue directly supports the mucosal cyanosis finding of methemoglobinemia. Skin tone assessed only from the visible facial skin.
